AGENDA

Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City
Clerk's Office. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public
comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk
at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Devine requested that staff ensure that electric vehicle charging stations
  are installed in the Montrose Area and the Northern Glendale. City Manager Golanian
  indicated that staff has been working on installing charging stations, primarily on Lot 3 north
  of Honolulu and the Montrose Shopping Park area.

  Councilmember Brotman attended the opening of the exhibit called “Lightning’s Lung” by
  artist Oliver Nowlin at the Museum of Neon Art. The exhibit will run through August 27, 2023.
  He also attended the opening of a new play called “Love and Information” at the Antaeus
  Theatre. The play will run through April 3, 2023. Additionally, Brotman attended an event
  hosted by GALAS (Gay and Lesbian Armenian Society) at the Glendale Central Library. At
  the event, the attendees heard from Lilit Martirosyan, a transgender activist, who talked
  about her struggle against transphobia and homophobia in Armenia. While attending an
  event by the Gay Man’s Chorus of Los Angeles (GMCLA), Brotman learned that the group is
  being kicked-out of the Glendale Alex Theatre and asked staff to investigate this issue.
  Devine seconded. Golanian indicated that he was told by staff that Alex Theatre is
  renegotiating the contract with the GMCLA. Director of Community Development Bradley
  Calvert indicated that SAS Entertainment manages the Alex Theatre and has had a policy in
  place that resident companies do not necessarily perform. He stated that SAS is working on
  the contract so that moving forward, GMCLA will not be classified as a resident company,
  but will be given a different title and will receive preferential treatment.

  Councilmember Najarian stated that the Alex Theatre put on an excellent show for Artsakh
  with the Children of Armenia Fund and commended Miles Williams, Founder and President
  of SAS Entertainment, for a well-attended event.

  Mayor Kassakhian thanked Mayor Pro Tem Najarian for running the meeting last week
  when he was out on city business. He and GWP staff attended the 2023 Legislative Rally,
  hosted by the American Public Power Association, where important issues were discussed
  such as the ones facing public utilities and to ensure that funds from the Inflation Reduction
  Act can be used and be beneficial for utilities nationwide. Some of the topics Kassakhian
  and GWP staff shared about were the city’s clean energy goals, updates on local projects
  and goals and ways to meet the SB-100 goals by year 2035 (ahead of year 2045). They
  also shared about how Glendale has been a leader in procuring clean energy resources,
  energy affordability, and addressing supply chain issues. Kassakhian congratulated the
  Glendale Latino Association (GLA) for a well-attended event and was honored to be the
  recipient of the “Man of the Year” award. He thanked the GLA for all the work they do for the
  community and urged anyone who wants to make donations to their organization to do so
  and help fund scholarships for Latino youth in the city. Kassakhian thanked and
  congratulated the Glendale Libraries for a well-attended inaugural book festival. He
  announced it was the kick-off of the little league season at Brand Park and wished everyone

  3
   who is playing to have a great season. Kassakhian congratulated Glendale Beautiful for a
  well-attended Arbor Day event at the Casa Adobe. He mentioned that Laura Stotler, a
  former Principal Planner of the City of Glendale, talked about the heritage of the city and its
  zoning policies.

  City Clerk Abajian announced that a new draft questionnaire for the 2030 Census was
  recently released by the Federal Office of Management and Budget (OMB). In the new
  proposed census questionnaire, the old racial and ethnic categories have been revamped
  and new categories are proposed. One of those new categories is the MENA category that
  includes subcategories such as Lebanese, Syrian, Iranian, etc. Previously these
  populations, including Armenians, were subsumed under the “white” racial category. This no
  longer will be the case. Abajian stated that the City of Glendale is home to the largest
  concentration of Armenians in the US and currently lacks comprehensive and meaningful
  data on its Armenian population. The Armenian population is largely absent from federal
  data and the lack of visibility in data has large ramifications for the Armenian community of
  Glendale including receiving services, funding, and support on issues spanning from
  housing, healthcare, business, to educational access. She stated she has been volunteering
  on a taskforce with ANCA Western Region to get public comments submitted on the draft
  2030 Census questionnaire asking the OMB to include an Armenian checkbox under the
  MENA category by the April 12th deadline for public comments. She requested that Council
  pass a resolution in support of the inclusion of an Armenian checkbox under the MENA
  category so that it could be submitted as a statement of support to the OMB. Najarian asked
  that the resolution be put on the Council agenda and Asatryan seconded.
